properties.natural_language: Before processing an authorization submitted by an external Transaction Submitter, the system MUST validate that the chain_id matches the current chain or is zero (wildcard).
Before accepting an authorization from an untrusted Transaction Submitter, the ECDSA signature (y_parity, r, s) MUST be validated as a cryptographically valid signature.
Authorization data crossing the trust boundary MUST include all required fields (chain_id, address, nonce, y_parity, r, s) and each field must be within its valid type range.
The Account code field stores raw bytecode without format validation at the Account level; any EOF or format validation occurs only at execution time, not at account creation or encoding.
When comparing authorization nonce (U64) with account nonce (Uint), both values MUST be treated as unsigned integers for comparison, despite differing type representations.

The storage_root parameter passed to encode_account MUST be a valid Merkle Patricia Trie root computed correctly from the account's storage; if this assumption is violated, state integrity is compromised.
ECDSA signature forgery for Authorization structures is computationally infeasible without knowledge of the private key.
The EMPTY_ACCOUNT constant is the sole canonical representation for non-existent accounts; no other byte pattern may be treated as equivalent to a non-existent account.

After ACTION-CREATE-ACCOUNT completes, the resulting account MUST have its nonce, balance, and code fields set to the specified values, transitioning from STATE-ACCOUNT-EMPTY to STATE-ACCOUNT-INITIALIZED.
After ACTION-ENCODE-ACCOUNT completes, the output MUST be a valid RLP encoding of (nonce, balance, storage_root, keccak256(code)).
After ACTION-RECOVER-AUTHORITY completes successfully, the recovered authority address MUST correspond to the actual signer of the authorization.

After ACTION-VALIDATE-ADDRESS-TYPE succeeds, the data is exactly 20 bytes; after ACTION-VALIDATE-ROOT-TYPE succeeds, the data is exactly 32 bytes; after ACTION-VALIDATE-BLOOM-TYPE succeeds, the data is exactly 256 bytes.
Before processing a block from a semi-trusted Block Proposer for fork activation, the block MUST meet Osaka fork activation criteria as defined by consensus rules.
Block data received from an untrusted Network Peer MUST undergo full structure validation (header and body) against Osaka block format before transaction processing begins.
No transactions from an untrusted network peer's block SHALL be executed until the block structure validation passes completely.
The Osaka fork activation criteria follow standard fork activation patterns with a designated block number or timestamp, consistent with prior forks.
Protocol requests processed in Osaka fork MUST follow the EIP-7685 pattern for system-level operations.
All previous fork rules (through Prague) MUST be correctly implemented and activated before Osaka fork activation can proceed.
Sufficient gas MUST be available for all operations before the Osaka state transition function begins execution; out-of-gas during critical state transitions must not leave state partially modified.
After ACTION-CHECK-FORK-BLOCK completes with activation criteria met, the system MUST transition to STATE-OSAKA-FORK-ACTIVE with new rules in effect.
After ACTION-VALIDATE-BLOCK-STRUCTURE completes successfully, the block header and body conform to Osaka block format.
After ACTION-PROCESS-TRANSACTIONS completes, all block transactions have been executed with state changes computed under Osaka rules.
After ACTION-UPDATE-STATE-TRIE completes, the Merkle Patricia trie has been updated with all state changes and a new state root has been computed.
After ACTION-ROLLBACK-STATE completes, all partial state changes from the failed operation have been fully reverted to the pre-operation snapshot.
After ACTION-APPLY-OSAKA-STATE-TRANSITION completes, the block has been fully processed using Osaka fork specifications.
Memory expansion and gas cost calculations are handled in separate modules (gas.py); memory.py handles only raw byte operations without gas awareness.
Memory positions specified as U256 are practically bounded by gas costs; the quadratic memory expansion gas cost makes very large positions economically infeasible.
When buffer_read encounters data beyond buffer boundaries, the utility method MUST use zero-padding (right_pad_zero_bytes) to fill the remaining bytes.
EVM memory MUST be initialized as an empty bytearray at the start of each execution context; no data from prior transactions or calls may leak into a new context.
Memory expansion gas MUST be charged before the write operation occurs; the write operation SHALL NOT proceed if gas charging fails.
Position and size parameters reaching memory functions MUST have been validated or gas-bounded by the calling context to prevent memory exhaustion or DoS.
After ACTION-MEMORY-WRITE completes, the memory contents at the specified position contain exactly the written bytes, and memory is in STATE-MEMORY-ALLOCATED.
After ACTION-MEMORY-READ completes, the returned bytes match exactly the memory contents at the specified position and size.

After ACTION-CHECK-BUFFER-BOUNDS determines that a read extends beyond the buffer, ACTION-APPLY-ZERO-PADDING MUST return data equal to the requested size, with in-bounds bytes from the buffer and remaining bytes as zero.
After ACTION-CHARGE-EXPANSION-GAS fails due to insufficient gas, the system transitions to STATE-OUT-OF-GAS and no memory modification occurs.
Before creating a subscription from an untrusted DApp Client, the subscription parameters MUST be validated and resource limits enforced to prevent subscription exhaustion attacks.
Before creating a filter from an untrusted HTTP RPC Client, filter parameters (from, to, hasReturnData) MUST be validated and filter count limits enforced per client.
Poll requests from an untrusted HTTP RPC Client MUST validate the filter ID and enforce rate limiting to prevent denial-of-service.
When invalid filter parameters are received, the system MUST return a standard JSON-RPC error response with error code -32602 (Invalid params).
When the underlying WebSocket connection is lost, all associated subscriptions MUST be automatically cleaned up; clients must resubscribe after reconnection.
Only transactions sealed (mined in blocks) after the creation of the filter SHALL be included in notifications; transactions pending in the pool at filter creation time are excluded.
The node correctly identifies which client submitted which transaction for subscription notifications; polling-based filtering cannot independently verify transaction origin.
WebSocket connections are expected to remain stable for the subscription duration; clients MUST handle reconnection and resubscription for any missed notifications.
Clients MUST correctly handle 'removed: true' notifications and update their state accordingly after chain reorganizations.
After ACTION-SUBSCRIBE completes, a unique subscription ID is returned and the node begins monitoring for matching transactions.
After ACTION-PUSH-NOTIFICATION completes, the client has received a notification containing the transaction hash and return data via WebSocket.
After ACTION-UNSUBSCRIBE completes, the subscription is terminated and no further notifications are sent for that subscription ID.
After ACTION-RETURN-COMPLETIONS, the accumulator is reset and the filter continues tracking new completions.
After ACTION-RESEND-WITH-REMOVED-FLAG completes, the client has been notified that a previously completed transaction was reversed by a chain reorganization.
After ACTION-CREATE-FILTER-INSTANCE completes, a filter with validated parameters is active and tracking transaction completions.
DUP operations MUST check for overflow (net stack effect +1, so stack length must be < 1024) and SWAP operations MUST check for sufficient depth but do not cause overflow (net effect 0).
The EVM stack limit of 1024 elements is enforced at the list level; no stack may exceed 1024 U256 values regardless of available host memory.
Stack operations (push, pop) are atomic and cannot be interrupted mid-operation; partial stack modifications are impossible.
All U256 values stored on the stack are within valid 256-bit unsigned integer bounds [0, 2^256 - 1].
After ACTION-PUSH succeeds on an empty stack, the stack transitions to STATE-STACK-PARTIAL with exactly 1 element.
After ACTION-POP succeeds on a stack with one element, the stack transitions to STATE-STACK-EMPTY with 0 elements and the popped value is returned.
After ACTION-POP on an empty stack, a StackUnderflowError is raised and execution enters the error handling path.
After ACTION-PUSH on a full stack (1024 elements), a StackOverflowError is raised and execution enters the error handling path.
After ACTION-HALT-EXECUTION triggered by a stack error, all remaining gas in the current context is consumed and execution is terminated.
After ACTION-CHECK-STACK-DEPTH succeeds, the stack has at least as many elements as the opcode requires for pops.
The stack length is always in the range [0, 1024]; it never goes negative or exceeds the maximum capacity.
Before creating a subscription from an untrusted User Application, subscription parameters MUST be validated including mutual exclusion of transaction/hash fields.
If a transaction is provided in the subscription request from an untrusted user, it MUST undergo the same validation as eth_sendRawTransaction before acceptance.
Transaction data submitted by an untrusted User/DApp for monitoring MUST pass full validation at the trust boundary before the node begins monitoring.
A subscription for a transaction hash that never appears in a block remains active indefinitely until the client explicitly unsubscribes.
Implementations MAY define their own resource limits for long-running subscriptions; clients MUST handle unexpected subscription termination gracefully.
The 'finalized' notification refers to consensus-layer finality on PoS chains; on chains without finality guarantees, this notification may never be sent.
The Ethereum node implementing transaction inclusion monitoring MUST maintain a mempool and be capable of tracking transaction propagation.
Users trust the node to accurately report transaction inclusion and reorg events; a malicious node could send false inclusion notifications.
Applications using reorg monitoring MUST implement appropriate logic to handle status:reorged notifications to avoid inconsistent state or double-spend vulnerabilities.
The transaction inclusion monitoring mechanism provides transparency (visibility into reorgs) but does NOT prevent reorg-based attacks; it is observational, not protective.
After ACTION-CREATE-SUBSCRIPTION completes, either a subscription ID is returned or a -32602 error is returned for invalid parameters.
After ACTION-SEND-INCLUSION-NOTIFICATION completes with includeReorgs=false, the subscription is automatically terminated.
After ACTION-SEND-INCLUSION-NOTIFICATION completes with includeReorgs=true, monitoring continues and the subscription remains active.
After ACTION-DETECT-REORG detects that a transaction's block has been orphaned, the system transitions to STATE-TX-REORGED-OUT and a reorg notification is sent.
After ACTION-WAIT-FOR-FINALITY detects block finalization, a status:finalized notification is sent indicating the transaction is irreversible.
After ACTION-VALIDATE-MUTUAL-EXCLUSION fails (both or neither transaction/hash provided), a -32602 error is returned and no subscription is created.
Node operators can observe which transactions users are monitoring, exposing monitoring patterns as a privacy consideration.
Protocol messages received from an untrusted Remote Peer Node MUST be validated against the 10MB devp2p packet size limit before processing.
NewPooledTransactionHashes messages from untrusted peers MUST contain at most 4096 hashes (128KB); GetPooledTransactions requests MUST contain at most 256 hashes.
Transactions retrieved via GetPooledTransactions from untrusted peers MUST be looked up only in the mempool (not disk) and MUST be returned in the same order as requested.
Nodes use implementation-specific heuristics (such as tracking recently sent hashes per peer or bloom filters) to determine which peers are unlikely to know about a transaction before announcing.
Partial or empty responses to GetPooledTransactions due to resource constraints are acceptable and SHALL NOT trigger peer disconnection.
Nodes SHOULD track recently received hash announcements and deduplicate requests to avoid redundant transaction fetches from duplicate announcements.
Peers are assumed to respond honestly to GetPooledTransactions with transactions matching the requested hashes; dishonest responses could enable transaction injection attacks.
All connected peers MUST support eth/65 protocol version for the hash announcement and retrieval mechanism to function correctly.

Attackers cannot flood the network with fake transaction hash announcements at scale; if violated, bandwidth amplification attacks become possible where small announcements trigger large retrieval requests.
After ACTION-BUILD-HASH-ANNOUNCEMENT completes, the resulting message contains up to 4096 transaction hashes within the 128KB limit.
After ACTION-BUILD-TX-REQUEST completes, the request contains up to 256 transaction hashes for retrieval.
After ACTION-LOOKUP-TX-POOL completes, only transactions currently in the mempool are returned; transactions on disk are not served.
Before accepting an EIP proposal from a semi-trusted EIP Author, the EIP specification MUST undergo evaluation by client teams for technical merit and readiness.
EIP proposals from authors MUST pass through the full review pipeline (proposed -> considered -> scheduled) before inclusion in the network upgrade.
Activation timestamps and epochs are initially TBD and are filled in by client teams closer to the upgrade date; they are undefined until formally set.
EIP categories follow EIP-7723 definitions: Scheduled, Considered, Declined, and Proposed for Inclusion.
All major Ethereum clients MUST implement the upgrade before the activation timestamp; failure to do so results in a potential network split.
Client teams coordinate honestly and follow the agreed-upon upgrade schedule; uncoordinated upgrades could cause network instability.
Network participants (validators, node operators) MUST have sufficient notice to upgrade their software before the activation time; insufficient notice causes forced forking.
After ACTION-EVALUATE-EIP completes, the EIP transitions to either STATE-EIP-CONSIDERED or remains in proposed state for further review.
After ACTION-SET-ACTIVATION-PARAMS completes, both the mainnet activation timestamp and beacon chain epoch are finalized.
After ACTION-DEPLOY-TESTNETS completes successfully, the upgrade is active on Sepolia and other testnets for validation.
After ACTION-DEPLOY-MAINNET completes, the Hegota upgrade is active on Ethereum mainnet.
Before processing signature components from an untrusted Signature Provider, the r value MUST be validated as a valid x-coordinate on the secp256k1 curve using Legendre symbol computation.
Before processing P-256 verification input from an untrusted Precompile Caller, the public key coordinates (x,y) MUST be validated to lie on the P-256 curve.
All signature and public key data from untrusted sources MUST have input bounds validated for the respective curve parameters before any modular arithmetic is performed.
The recovery identifier v MUST be within the expected range [0, 1, 27, 28]; values outside this range are handled by the coincurve library which raises appropriate errors.
A 'valid x-coordinate' on secp256k1 means the value x satisfies: x^3 + 7 (mod p) is a quadratic residue, verified by Legendre symbol computation.
The coincurve library implementation is assumed to be cryptographically correct and secure; incorrect ECDSA operations could allow signature forgery.
All elliptic curve arithmetic is performed modulo respective field primes without integer overflow in the underlying implementation.
An attacker cannot find collisions in the message hash (keccak256/SHA256) that would allow signature reuse across different messages.
After ACTION-VALIDATE-R-ON-CURVE succeeds, the r value is confirmed as a valid secp256k1 curve point x-coordinate.
After ACTION-VALIDATE-R-ON-CURVE fails, an InvalidSignatureError is raised and no recovery is attempted.
After ACTION-RECOVER-PUBLIC-KEY succeeds, the recovered uncompressed public key is exactly 64 bytes (prefix excluded).
After ACTION-CHECK-POINT-ON-CURVE succeeds for P-256, the public key point satisfies y^2 = x^3 + ax + b (mod p).
After ACTION-VERIFY-SIGNATURE succeeds, the P-256 ECDSA signature has been cryptographically verified as valid for the given message and public key.
After ACTION-RAISE-INVALID-SIG-ERROR, an InvalidSignatureError has been propagated to the calling context.

Before accepting a blob transaction from an untrusted Transaction Submitter, the system MUST validate: (1) EIP-4844 format, (2) non-nil 'to' address, (3) valid secp256k1 signature, (4) at least one blob, (5) versioned hash prefix 0x01, and (6) sufficient sender balance.
Blob transaction announcements from an untrusted Peer Node MUST only contain hash, type, and size; full transaction data MUST be retrieved and validated separately.
Blob data received from the untrusted P2P network gossip layer MUST be verified via KZG commitment validation before being treated as available.
A 'valid blob' means: correct KZG commitment, correct format (4096 field elements), within size limits, and proof verifies cryptographically.
Nodes MAY prune blob data after 4096 epochs (~18 days) but SHOULD retain it for at least this period; exact pruning behavior is implementation-defined.
Blob transaction mempool replacement requires both execution and blob fees to meet the 1.1x bump requirement over the existing transaction.
The KZG trusted setup ceremony was performed correctly and the toxic waste was destroyed; if compromised, attackers could forge KZG proofs for arbitrary data.
Attackers cannot perform discrete log in BLS12-381 curve or break the KZG polynomial commitment scheme.
The network can handle approximately 0.75 MB/block additional bandwidth from blob data without causing congestion that delays block propagation.
Rollups and data consumers MUST retrieve blob data within the 18-day availability window; failure to do so results in irreversible data loss.
After ACTION-VALIDATE-TX-FORMAT succeeds and all subsequent checks pass, the blob transaction transitions to STATE-BLOB-TX-VALIDATED.
After ACTION-COMPUTE-VERSIONED-HASH completes, the result is a 32-byte hash with the first byte being VERSIONED_HASH_VERSION_KZG (0x01) followed by sha256(commitment)[1:].
After ACTION-VERIFY-KZG-PROOF succeeds, the blob data is cryptographically verified to match its commitment, and transitions to STATE-BLOB-AVAILABLE.
After ACTION-CALC-EXCESS-BLOB-GAS completes, the result equals max(0, parent.excess_blob_gas + parent.blob_gas_used - TARGET_BLOB_GAS_PER_BLOCK).
After ACTION-CALC-BLOB-BASE-FEE completes, the blob base fee is determined by the exponential formula fake_exponential(MIN_BASE_FEE_PER_BLOB_GAS, excess_blob_gas, BLOB_BASE_FEE_UPDATE_FRACTION).
After ACTION-DEDUCT-BLOB-FEE completes, the blob fee (blob_base_fee * total_blob_gas) is permanently burned from the sender's balance and is not refunded on transaction failure.
After ACTION-CHECK-MAX-FEE-COVERAGE fails (max_fee < base_fee), the transaction is rejected with STATE-FEE-INSUFFICIENT.
After ACTION-CHARGE-PRECOMPILE-GAS succeeds (gas >= 50,000), the precompile proceeds to parse the 192-byte input.
After ACTION-VERIFY-KZG-POINT succeeds in the precompile, FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB and BLS_MODULUS are returned as a 64-byte output.
After ACTION-CHECK-INDEX-BOUNDS determines the index is out of bounds, BLOBHASH pushes bytes32(0) onto the stack.
After ACTION-FETCH-VERSIONED-HASH succeeds, the 32-byte versioned hash from tx.blob_versioned_hashes[index] is pushed onto the EVM stack.
The total blob_gas_used in a block MUST NOT exceed MAX_BLOB_GAS_PER_BLOCK (786,432), corresponding to a maximum of 6 blobs per block.
Blob transactions MUST have a non-nil 'to' address; contract creation via blob transactions is forbidden.
Every blob_versioned_hash in a blob transaction MUST start with VERSIONED_HASH_VERSION_KZG (0x01) byte prefix.
A blob transaction MUST contain at least one blob (len(blob_versioned_hashes) >= 1).
Blob gas cost per blob is fixed at GAS_PER_BLOB (131,072); total blob gas equals GAS_PER_BLOB * len(blob_versioned_hashes).
